subject: Prompt/Response Custody and Escrow — proposed operational path
messages:
From: Claire Hsu <claire@medonix.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Medonix Procurement <procurement@medonix.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model-improvement opt-out + custody for prompts/responses (RFP MDX-8342)

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the demo last week — Medonix legal and procurement asked me to follow up on a few points we need in the DPA/addendum for our risk committee. High level asks: 

- Confirm whether Redwood will use customer-provided prompts or generated responses to improve or retrain any models (we need an explicit opt-out or a clause that prohibits derivative training).
- Ownership: we need language that clarifies customer ownership of prompts and of generated responses and any derivative access by third parties.
- Operational custody/escrow: the committee wants a mechanism to obtain a time-stamped copy of interaction transcripts (prompts + responses) on demand for audits and e-discovery — ideally a push to our SFTP or a signed escrow with an audit log.
- Subprocessors and transfers: provide the up-to-date subprocessors list and a short note on whether any subprocessor will process data outside the US.

Attached is the procurement questionnaire (excerpted) — highlighted the items we need answered. Can you confirm whether Redwood can meet these requirements and an estimated timeline to deliver artifacts (DPA language, subprocessor CSV, ops runbook)?

RFP ref: MDX-8342.

Thanks,
Claire Hsu
Senior Contracts Manager
Medonix Health

Attachment: MDX-RFP-questionnaire.pdf (attachment stub)

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Claire Hsu <claire@medonix.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, david_kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model-improvement opt-out + custody for prompts/responses (RFP MDX-8342)

Claire — thanks for the clear list. We can meet the requirements but want to align on exact wording and operational mechanics. Quick summary of what I can commit to right now: 

- Model improvement opt-out: we can include an explicit addendum clause that prevents Redwood from using customer prompts/responses to train or improve models unless the customer provides opt-in consent. Draft language attached.
- Ownership: we propose to state that the customer retains ownership of prompts and generated responses; Redwood holds a limited license to process them solely to provide the service.
- Escrow/export: operationally we can deliver a push export to an encrypted SFTP endpoint (per-customer prefix) on a scheduled cadence or on-demand for audits. We can also provide an escrow option (time-stamped, signed archive) if the customer requires an independent custody provider.
- Subprocessors: we will share a current CSV and mark locations; if any subprocessor processes data outside the US we will highlight them and provide SOC2/hearing evidence where available.

I'm looping in Kimberly (legal) and David (ops) to confirm the precise contractual language and the runbook we would provide. Attached: DPA_Addendum_ModelOptOut.pdf (draft), ops_export_runbook.md (ops summary), subprocessors_list.csv (current snapshot).

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly to review/flag any contract redlines.
2) David to confirm the SFTP/residency runbook and delivery timeline (we can do a first export in a POC window within 5 business days once credentials are provided).
3) I will share the revised addendum and a DocuSign link for execution.

Can you confirm whether Medonix prefers on-demand exports (manual) or a scheduled nightly export during the POC?

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_Addendum_ModelOptOut.pdf (attachment stub), ops_export_runbook.md (attachment stub), subprocessors_list.csv (attachment stub)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Claire Hsu <claire@medonix.com>
Cc: david_kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model-improvement opt-out + custody for prompts/responses (RFP MDX-8342)

Sergio / Claire — quick legal read and a few redline asks: 

1) Wording: please replace ambiguous "improve or train" with a single defined term, e.g., "derivative-model-training". The clause should prohibit Redwood and its subprocessors from using Customer Interaction Data for any derivative-model-training or model parameter updates unless Customer gives express written consent.

2) IP & Output: we need an explicit sentence that states "Customer owns all Customer Input and Generated Outputs; Redwood shall have only the limited rights necessary to provide the Service and shall not assert ownership of Generated Outputs."

3) Proof of safeguards: procurement will want evidence. Requesting the following artifacts from Ops: 
   - current subprocessors_list.csv with country column and processing purpose;
   - confirmation of KMS model for customer namespace (e.g., CMEK/HSM vs platform-managed);
   - a short example of an export manifest (what fields and checksums are included) and sample retention SLA.

4) Data residency: Claire — if you need a strict onshore-only processing commitment for the interaction transcripts, call that out now. We can propose an onshore routing option but it may limit burst capacity.

From a legal perspective, we should also commit to a 3rd-party attestation (SOC2) and a subcontractor attest signature pipeline for subprocessors. I will prepare contract redlines and aim to send them by EOD tomorrow.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

(On Wed, 16 Jul 2025 at 10:02, sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com> wrote:)
> Claire — thanks for the clear list. We can meet the requirements but want to align on exact wording and operational mechanics...

Attachment referenced: legal_redlines_outline.docx (attachment stub)

From: david_kim <david@redwood.com>
To: Claire Hsu <claire@medonix.com>, sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jul 2025 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Model-improvement opt-out + custody for prompts/responses (MDX-8342)

Claire — ops follow-up with concrete operational commitments and timelines: 

1) Escrow/export options: we offer two patterns:
   a) Scheduled encrypted SFTP push: nightly (UTC) ZIP archives written to your provided SFTP with customer-prefixed directories. Each archive includes a manifest.csv with checksums, start/end timestamps, and per-session metadata.
   b) On-demand export: triggered via a signed API call or via a procurement request; typical turnaround for a single export is 8–24 hours depending on size.

2) Retention & format: exported archives can be held on your SFTP for your retention policy; we can also retain a single encrypted copy in our escrow for 7 years if you request an independent escrow provider. Exports contain prompts, full responses, timestamps, session IDs, and SHA256 checksums.

3) Residency & subprocessors: current subprocessors_list.csv (attached) flags two vendors who operate EU-based processing for model-ops telemetry (non-customer-content). For customer interaction exports we can route processing onshore (US-CENTRAL) for the POC.

4) Key management: we support CMEK via customer-provided keys (Cloud KMS/HSM) for storage encryption on exported archives; if you require HSM-backed keys we can route the export buckets accordingly — note this will add 2–3 days to the initial POC setup to exchange credentials and do validation.

5) Ephemeral caching: to be clear operationally, interaction KV caches are ephemeral and not persisted to long-term storage unless exported in the archive; we will provide an ops runbook with the cache TTLs and retention guardrails.

6) Timeline: once Medonix provides SFTP credentials and confirms onshore routing preference, Ops can deliver an initial POC export within 5 business days. Legal redlines (Kimberly) + signed addendum via DocuSign will be required before we enable scheduled exports in production.

Links and artifacts:
- Ops runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBExampleOpsRunbook
- Initial DPA addendum (draft): https://drive.google.com/file/d/0DPA_Addendum_ModelOptOut (attached to email)
- DocuSign to execute addendum: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/embedded?envelopeId=5f3a-example

If this sounds good, Sergio — please send the preferred export cadence back to Claire and I will prepare the POC checklist and a sample manifest to attach.

David Kim
Director, Platform Operations — Redwood Inference

Attachment: sample_manifest_example.csv (attachment stub)
